title: Authorization Fail-Open Default
pattern: Exception or error-handling blocks in authentication/authorization code returning `true` or mapping to "allow" if policy lookups or network connections fail.
why_bad: In conditions of resource exhaustion, disk errors, or temporary network failure, the security checks collapse and default to permitting access, allowing attackers to bypass authentication entirely.
detection: An `Err` handler or panic recovery block inside an authorization function returning `true` or matching to a lenient permission set.
fix: Ensure all authorization paths default to "deny all". Access must be explicitly granted; any failure during lookup must trigger immediate denial.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 8, p. 158.
